title: Fog on the River
text: A thick fog covers the river from the evening. No customs man will see a barge tonight.

title: A Leaking Hull
text: The barge is taking on water. Half the night goes on bailing and hunting for the hole.

title: A Search at the Lock
text: The customs man at the lock studies the papers for a long time. In the end he waves you on, but it cost everyone's nerves.

title: The Wharf Inn
text: The innkeeper at the landing stands a round. He says the river watch goes upstream tomorrow.

title: A Barrel from the Current
text: You fish a barrel from someone else's cargo out of the current. There is good wine inside.

title: A Snapped Mooring
text: A gale snaps the mooring and the barge drifts into the dark. You catch it only at the shallows.

title: An Honest Ferryman
text: An old ferryman asks what you are carrying. When he hears the price of silence, he stops asking.

title: A Gift for the Customs Man
text: A customs man asks for a 'sample' of the goods for his wife. Better to give than to explain.

title: A Fair Wind
text: The wind blows from the right quarter. The barge moves faster than ever.

title: Rats in the Hold
text: Rats have got into the food sacks. Some of the food has to be thrown out.

title: Rivals on the Water
text: A strange boat follows you all night. In the morning it vanishes round a bend.

title: Payment in Advance
text: The buyer sends an advance for the next run. The crew takes it as a good sign.

title: Mules in the Snow
text: Snow has buried the path. The contraband mules wade belly-deep, and one falls into a drift with its packs.

title: The Dwarf Watchpost
text: The dwarf pass wardens go through the packs with stony faces. In the end they take a toll and let you pass.

title: The Pass Shelter
text: The stone shelter is empty and dry. The crew sleeps warm for the first time in days.

title: A Mountain Guide
text: An old guide knows a path no watchpost covers, and charges well for it.

title: Avalanche
text: Thunder above, and an avalanche buries the road behind you. There is no way back, but nobody is following either.

title: Traders from the Hold
text: Dwarf traders pay silver for lowland tobacco. The crew sells what they kept for themselves.

title: The Buyer Haggles
text: The buyer cuts the rate by a fifth, saying times are hard and the customs men are sniffing about.

title: A Letter from the Buyer
text: The buyer writes that they will take any cargo you bring. The skipper reads it with a smile.

title: A Retired Customs Man
text: An old customs man in the inn tells how he looked the other way for years. For a round he says who takes bribes today.

title: Sour Wine
text: A cask of wine has soured on the way. Nobody will buy it, so the crew drinks it themselves.

title: An Informer at the Docks
text: Someone is telling the customs men about your runs. The skipper orders a change of route for a few days.

title: A Borrowed Boat
text: A fisherman lends a boat for a few shillings and asks no questions.

title: A Storm on the River
text: A gale raises waves on the river. The barge stays at the bank and the crew holds the ropes all night.

title: An Old Wreck
text: An old wreck lies by the bank. A few sacks of salt are left in its hold.

title: A Quarrel over Shares
text: Two smugglers argue over their share of the last run. The skipper splits it evenly and tells them to be quiet.

title: The Boatmen's Feast
text: Boatmen from all along the river celebrate their patron's day. The crew drinks with them and learns where the patrols are.

title: A New Customs Post
text: A new customs post stands on the route. You will need another way or another customs man.

title: A Stowaway
text: A runaway journeyman is hiding among the cargo and pays for passage with what is in their pockets.

title: Stores from the Fair
text: Hardtack and salt meat are cheap at the fair. The purser stocks up.

title: A Good Year for Wine
text: The vineyards have done well, and city prices rise with every toll. Cargoes will be worth more this year.

title: A Shoal in the Dark
text: The barge scrapes over sand. A few more fathoms and it will be stuck for good.
okText: The helmsman turns the barge a hair's breadth from the rocks and takes it into deep water.

title: A Raid at the Landing
text: At night someone tries to cut the barge loose and take the cargo.
okText: The boatman wakes first and throws the attacker into the river.

title: A Lantern on the Bank
text: A lantern blinks on the bank. It may be a signal, or a trap.
okText: The lookout recognises the uniforms of the river watch and the barge hides in the reeds.

title: A Missing Seal
text: The bill of lading lacks a guild seal. In the morning you must pass the customs house.
okText: The forger carves a seal from a turnip and by dawn the papers look new.

title: A Merchant with a Surplus
text: A merchant at the landing wants to be rid of a stock of dried fish.
okText: The purser haggles until midnight and buys at half the price.

title: A Hidden Compartment
text: Someone from another crew saw where you hide the goods.
okText: The smuggler moves the cargo to a new hiding place before anyone can inform.

title: A Ford in the Gorge
text: A rushing stream cuts the path and the mules are afraid to enter the water.
okText: The helmsman finds the shallows and leads the animals across one by one.

title: A Rope on the Cliff
text: The packs must be hauled up to a ledge on a rope.
okText: The boatman hauls the rope alone and by nightfall everything is up.

title: Movement on the Road
text: Men in watch colours appear on the road.
okText: The lookout spots them first and the crew hides the cargo before they ride up.

title: A New Seal
text: The customs house has changed its seal. The old papers are worthless.
okText: That same night the forger copies the new seal from someone else's bill of lading.

title: Muddled Accounts
text: The buyer claims the last cargo has already been paid for.
okText: The purser shows the accounts to the shilling and the buyer pays the rest.

title: A False Bottom
text: The customs men announce a search of every cart and pack.
okText: The smuggler moves the goods into false-bottomed chests and the search finds nothing.
